options.content: Encrypts data travelling between the browser and the web server
options.rationale: Correct: shown by a padlock in the address bar.

options.content: Makes web pages load even when there is no internet connection at all
options.rationale: HTTPS still needs a connection.

options.content: Checks every link on a page for errors
options.rationale: That is link testing.

options.content: Compresses the images on a web page
options.rationale: That is image optimisation.

explanation: HTTPS encrypts data in transit using the site's digital certificate.

options.content: A service storing a site's files on an internet server
options.rationale: Correct: visitors request pages from the host's server.

options.content: The person who designs the site's logo
options.rationale: That is a graphic designer.

options.content: A plugin that adds a contact form to the pages of a website
options.rationale: That is a plugin.

options.content: The name typed in the address bar
options.rationale: That is the domain name.

explanation: Hosting keeps the website's files on a web server that is always online.

stem: Why should the plugins of a CMS website be kept updated?

options.content: Old plugins change the site's colours
options.rationale: Colours are set by the theme.

options.content: Updates register the domain name again
options.rationale: Domain registration is separate.

options.content: Updates fix security weaknesses that attackers look for
options.rationale: Correct: out-of-date plugins are a common way in.

options.content: Plugins stop working on phones after a month unless updated
options.rationale: Plugins do not expire like that.

explanation: Keeping software updated closes known security holes.

stem: Which developer tool feature shows a message such as "404 not found" for an image that failed to load?

options.content: The bookmarks bar
options.rationale: Bookmarks store addresses.

options.content: The console or network view
options.rationale: Correct: they list errors and failed downloads.

options.content: The browser's history
options.rationale: History lists visited pages.

options.content: The print preview
options.rationale: Print preview shows the printed layout.

explanation: The console shows errors; the network view shows every file and its status.

stem: What is the main reason for giving a website's authors permission only to write posts, and not to install plugins?

options.content: Authors cannot type quickly enough to install plugins
options.rationale: Speed is not the reason.

options.content: Plugins can only be installed on Fridays
options.rationale: There is no such rule.

options.content: Authors would otherwise see a different theme on every page
options.rationale: Permissions do not change the theme.

options.content: Each user gets only the access they need, which limits damage
options.rationale: Correct: the principle of least privilege.

explanation: Careful permissions limit what each account can change.

stem: A form accepts an age from 10 to 60. Which value is the **boundary** value that should be rejected at the top of the range?

options.rationale: This is the largest value that should be accepted.
Correct: the smallest value above the range.
This is the lower boundary, which should be accepted.

options.content: sixty
options.rationale: This is abnormal (wrong type) data, not a boundary value.

explanation: Boundary testing uses 60 (largest accepted) and 61 (smallest rejected).
hints: Which data is just outside the allowed range?

stem: A site uses HTTPS. Why is it still not completely secure?

options.content: HTTPS makes all passwords visible to visitors
options.rationale: HTTPS encrypts data; it does not reveal passwords.

options.content: HTTPS switches off the input validation on every form on the site
options.rationale: The two are independent.

options.content: It protects data in transit, not weak passwords or old plugins
options.rationale: Correct: other measures are needed.

options.content: HTTPS only works on desktop computers
options.rationale: It works on all devices.

explanation: Combine HTTPS with strong passwords, updates, validation, permissions and backups.
hints: HTTPS protects data in transit only.

stem: Why must a web server check form input even when the browser has already checked it?

options.content: Browsers never check the input that is typed into a form by a user
options.rationale: Many browsers check input, but it can be bypassed.

options.content: The server checks only the spelling of names
options.rationale: Server checks cover format, range and harmful content.

options.content: Checking twice makes the page load faster
options.rationale: Extra checks do not speed up loading.

options.content: Attackers can bypass browser checks and send data directly
options.rationale: Correct: server-side validation is the real protection.

explanation: Browser checks help honest users; the server must validate and sanitise everything it receives.
hints: What could happen if a form passes typed text straight to the database?

stem: A website should be tested in several browsers and on phones as well as computers.
explanation: True. Layout and features can behave differently on different browsers and screen sizes.

stem: Changes made to a page in the browser's developer tools are saved permanently on the web server.
explanation: False. They are temporary and only in that browser; the real files must be corrected and uploaded.

stem: Match each security measure to the threat it reduces.

left.content: Strong admin password and two-factor authentication

right.content: Harmful code typed into a form
Losing the site after it is hacked
Form data being read if it is intercepted
Attackers taking over the administrator account

explanation: Each measure targets a specific threat.

stem: Put the steps for publishing a website in order by choosing the correct step for each position.

choices: Upload the files to the web server
Upload the files to the web server
Upload the files to the web server
Upload the files to the web server

accepted: Upload the files to the web server

explanation: 1. Register a domain name. 2. Choose web hosting. 3. Upload the files to the web server. 4. Test the live site.
hints: You need a name before hosting can be linked to it; test last.

stem: Name the protocol that encrypts data between a browser and a web server and shows a padlock in the address bar.
Describe **two** security measures a developer should use for a school website's administrator login. [4]

points.description: so that attackers cannot guess or reuse the password to take control
Limit login attempts / CAPTCHA / HTTPS on the login page
so that automated guessing is slowed / the password cannot be read if intercepted

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Use a strong, unique password with two-factor authentication, so an attacker cannot guess the password and take control; and limit login attempts, so automated programs cannot keep guessing.

hints: Give a measure and its reason, twice.

stem: Describe **four** tests that should be carried out on a website before it is published. [4]

points.description: Click every link / navigation item to check none is broken
Test forms with normal, abnormal and boundary data
Check layout on different screen sizes / devices / browsers
Check loading speed / images and alt text / spelling / HTTPS / accessibility

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Click every link to check none is broken; enter normal, abnormal and boundary data in each form; view the pages on phones and computers in different browsers; and check how quickly pages load.

hints: Think about links, forms, layout and devices.

stem: Nyasha is testing a club registration form. The age box accepts whole numbers from 10 to 60.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Give a **normal** test value for the age.
parts.explanation: Any whole number from 11 to 59 is normal data (10 and 60 are boundary values).

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Which is **abnormal** data for the age?

options.rationale: Boundary.
Boundary.

options.content: twelve
options.rationale: Correct: text where a number is expected.
Normal.

parts.explanation: Abnormal data is of the wrong type or clearly invalid.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: State the boundary value that should be rejected at the **bottom** of the range.
parts.explanation: 9 is the largest value below the range.
parts.workedSolution:
1. The smallest accepted value is 10.
2. The value just below it, 9, must be rejected.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: On a phone, the form's Submit button is cut off at the edge of the screen. Describe how Nyasha could use browser developer tools to find the cause.

points.description: Use responsive mode to view the page at phone width
Inspect the element / its HTML and CSS to find the width setting causing the problem (then correct the real file)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: She switches the developer tools to responsive mode at phone width, then inspects the button and its container to see which CSS width is too large, and corrects it in her files.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: True or false: after correcting the fault, Nyasha should run the test again.

explanation: Normal 11-59; abnormal "twelve"; boundary rejected 9; responsive mode and inspect; retest.
hints: Developer tools: inspect, console, network, responsive mode.

stem: Farai has finished a website for his family's guest house in Nyanga on his laptop and now wants to publish it.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Describe the steps Farai must take to publish the site.

points.description: Register a domain name (e.g. a .co.zw name)
Buy / choose web hosting and upload the files to the web server (control panel / secure FTP)
Install a certificate for HTTPS and test the live site

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: He registers a domain name, chooses a web host and uploads his files to its server using the control panel, then installs a certificate for HTTPS and tests the live site.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: The site has a booking form. Evaluate **three** security measures Farai should use.

points.description: HTTPS so guests' details are encrypted in transit
Validate and sanitise form input on the server so harmful data is rejected
Strong admin password / updates / backups, each with a reason

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: HTTPS encrypts guests' details as they are sent; server-side validation rejects harmful or invalid input; and regular backups mean the site can be restored if it is attacked.

explanation: Domain, hosting, upload, HTTPS, test; HTTPS, validation and backups with reasons.
hints: Pair each measure with its reason.
